about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2014 only.

rows.detail: ZONING INCENTIVE PAYMENT $99,000.00 (new line, absent in FY2013);

rows.table: Special revenue funds: grants, gifts, revolving and enterprise accounts
rows.detail: Fully readable, but a dormant fund prints only its opening and closing figures with the two middle columns absent, so a naive parse will mis-assign them.
That is an explicit record of what is MISSING from the year, which FY2013 does not provide.
FY2013's version of this table (page 83) is unreadable - the row labels are entirely absent.

Real operating data with no table around it: 730 properties connected and another 390 with access but not connected; forty new connections in FY2014; $656,440 billed in quarterly sewer bills; $53,730 of prior year delinquencies added to property tax bills; sixteen properties assessed privilege fees; 19 grease trap establishments; 10 pumping stations and 10 generators; approximately 76% of sewage discharged to Leominster and 24% to Fitchburg; a $5,000 minimum fine for illegal connections; service outsourced to Small Water Systems Services of Littleton from August 2013.
Named-disease case counts for one town in one year - not something a budget document would normally carry, and completely absent from the FY2013 report.
The standing caveat 'TERMS ARE FOR ONE YEAR UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED.' is reprinted at the top of every one of the five pages.
The same all-caps explanation about the Registry of Vital Records is reprinted verbatim from the FY2013 report, so both years carry counts only and no names.

rows.table: Exemptions, abatements and overlay, five years
rows.detail: The row heading 'Charges to 6/30/2010' is reprinted verbatim in the FY2014 report even though it now carries FY2014 figures - a stale label carried across at least two years.

Page 96 publishes exactly the number that dollars cannot give you - out-of-district special education placements COUNTED and split by type: 'seven are serviced in Collaborative Placements, thirteen are in Day Placements and six are in Residential Placements'. The FY2013 report gives the same count for the prior year (seventeen day, five residential, no collaborative category), so the two reports together are two consecutive years of placement counts.

The Sewer Commissioner seat was won with eleven votes - six in Precinct A, four in B, one in C, none in D - against 1,199 blanks. The winner's name is printed with '**' as elected, on a ballot where the office drew 38 write-ins.

Question 5 on the November 2014 ballot appears in Precinct B only, and the report prints it that way with dashes in the other three precincts, because Precinct B is Lunenburg's only precinct in the 3rd Worcester District. A reader who did not know that would read the dashes as missing data.

The table of contents lists four bodies as 'no report' rather than leaving them out - Agricultural Commission, Conservation Commission, Cultural Council and Veterans Agent. The report explicitly documents its own gaps.

The FY2014 trust funds table carries account numbers and fund NAMES; the FY2013 one carries perfectly clean rows of money with no names at all in its text layer. The FY2014 opening balances match the FY2013 closing balances, so this report is the key that labels the previous year's unlabelled table.

Community Policing grants from federal fiscal 1996, 1997 and 1998 are still open in FY2014 at $0.66, $1.97 and $6.55 - the identical balances they carried in FY2013, sixteen to eighteen years after the grants ended.

A single January 2014 Special Town Meeting article, passed on a 5-1 Finance Committee recommendation and confirmed by a 1,414-543 debt exclusion vote on a 28% turnout, authorised $72,975,321 of borrowing - more than three times the town's entire existing long-term debt of $22.1M and more than twice its annual operating budget.

Two tables on the SAME PAGE (35) use different tax rates for the same fiscal year: the Valuation and Tax History table gives FY2013 as 17.30 while the New Growth Revenue table applies 16.83 to FY2013 - and the FY2013 report's own history table ends its rate series at 16.83, so the two years' history tables are offset by one year against each other.

rows.table: Valuation and tax rate history, nine years
rows.detail: The FY2013 report's own version of this history table ends its tax-rate run at 16.83, i.e. it is offset by one year against this one.

rows.table: Lunenburg Primary School faculty and staff roster
rows.detail: The three-column layout interleaves in the text layer, so 'Central Office: / Elaine Blaisdell - Principal / First Grade: / 1A - Michael Courtemanche / Special Education / Karen Rash' is three different columns' worth of one horizontal band - reconstructing requires x-positions.

rows.table: Lunenburg High School MCAS results, grades 8 and 10
rows.detail: MIND THE HEADINGS: the grade 8 table is labelled 2014 and the grade 10 table is labelled 2013 - two different testing years printed side by side in the same report.

IMPORTANT: like FY2013's report, this prints a FORWARD budget - FY2015 - inside the FY2014 report, so this document contains three different fiscal years of figures (FY2014 actuals, FY2015 voted, and FY2013 comparatives in the assessor tables).
School Committee meets twice a month in two different buildings.
Extraction caveat: because it is three column-pairs on one line, a naive line parse will merge three different accounts.

rows.table: New growth revenue by fiscal year
rows.detail: Also the FY2012 figure differs from the FY2013 report: here FY2012 added valuation is 27,729,619 / 448,111 new revenue / +137.43%, whereas the FY2013 report's series has no such row.
NOTE the narrative on the very next page says '26.4 square miles' - the two pages disagree.

The whole Monty Tech section (pages 111-129) is not written for this report at all - it is the regional school district's OWN separately designed '2013 - 2014 Annual Report', cover page and address block included, dropped in whole. That is why it is the only OCR'd content in an otherwise born-digital document: it was scanned back in from a printed booklet.
